name: Secondary school
description: Ages roughly 12-18 in secondary school, teacher-led, often working toward a syllabus or exam. Longer lessons, more abstraction, graded assessment.
tone: clear, respectful, a little more formal; assume growing independence

session.notes: A class period; homework may extend it.

assessment_style: Mix of formative checks and graded, syllabus-aligned assessment; exam practice where relevant.

privacy.consent_notes: Minors: pending_review by default; older teens may share questions only with guardian-set consent.

language_note: School language of instruction; subject vocabulary introduced explicitly.

what_if_wrong.reading_level: Too high: a learner cannot decode the text and disengages; too low: an adult feels patronised. A LEARNER profile's reading_level always overrides this default.
what_if_wrong.tone: A mismatched tone (jokey for a compliance course, stern for a child) breaks trust. INPUT/SOURCE tone wins over this default.
what_if_wrong.session: Sessions longer than the real attention window lose the learner near the end; too short and a topic never resolves. MP-11 uses this as the lesson time unit; an explicit duration in the brief overrides it.
what_if_wrong.guide_role: Assuming an adult is present when none is (or the reverse) makes instructions unusable. If LEARNER says otherwise, LEARNER wins.
what_if_wrong.assessment_style: A high-stakes graded style on a low-stakes context (or vice versa) distorts pace and anxiety. Named exams in the brief override this.
what_if_wrong.delivery_media: Assuming a screen where there is none (or bandwidth that is not there) makes content undeliverable. A modifier (offline-first, low-bandwidth) narrows this further.
what_if_wrong.privacy: Treating a minor context as adult can publish a child's data; the floor is pending_review for minors and visibility is never relaxed below the profile's default.
what_if_wrong.language_note: Ignoring the dominant language or a second-language audience produces text no one here can read. LEARNER.languages[0] wins.
